title: Tricuspid valve disease surgery: functional regurgitation, ring annuloplasty, carcinoid and Ebstein anomaly
subject: ss-ctvs

Kirklin/Barratt-Boyes Cardiac Surgery 4e Ch 16 (Tricuspid Valve Disease)

steps.say: Functional tricuspid regurgitation accounts for over 85 to 90 percent of surgical tricuspid pathology. Left-sided heart disease elevates pulmonary pressures, causing progressive right ventricular dilatation. As the ventricle enlarges, severe annular dilatation prevents leaflet coaptation despite structurally normal leaflets.
steps.tx: Over 85 to 90 percent of clinical cases represent **functional tricuspid regurgitation**, developing secondary to left-sided valvular lesions, chronic pulmonary hypertension, and **right ventricular enlargement**. As the right ventricle remodels and dilates, marked **annular dilatation** displaces papillary muscles, producing severe secondary regurgitation.

steps.say: Perform concomitant tricuspid annuloplasty whenever left-sided valve surgery is indicated for severe tricuspid regurgitation. Guidelines give a Class I recommendation for severe regurgitation, and Class IIa for mild to moderate regurgitation when the annular diameter exceeds 40 millimetres. Addressing the tricuspid valve prevents late right heart failure.
steps.tx: A **guideline recommendation** assigns a Class I indication for **concomitant annuloplasty** during left-sided valve surgery in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation. It also provides a Class IIa indication for mild-to-moderate regurgitation when intraoperative **annular diameter** exceeds 40 mm (or 21 mm/m2).

rows: Class I recommendation for concomitant repair
Class IIa recommendation for concomitant repair
Class IIb or observation; medical surveillance

steps.say: Tricuspid annular dilatation is anatomically asymmetrical. Dilatation occurs predominantly along the anterior and posterior leaflet attachments. In contrast, the septal leaflet annulus remains stable and constant because it is anchored firmly to the central fibrous skeleton of the heart.
steps.tx: Annular stretching occurs almost exclusively along the **anterior annulus** and posterior annular segments. In contrast, the **septal leaflet** attachment remains structurally fixed and undilated because it is firmly anchored into the fibrous trigone and central **fibrous skeleton** of the heart, guiding surgical ring sizing.

left.title: Anterior and Posterior Annulus
points: Undergoes massive elongation during right ventricular dilatation
Target of plication and ring remodeling during repair

right.title: Septal Annulus Segment
points: Anchored directly into central fibrous skeleton
Maintains constant dimension across right heart enlargement
Serves as anatomical reference for measuring annuloplasty ring size

steps.say: A rigid or semi-rigid prosthetic ring achieves superior durability compared to suture techniques. Historical suture annuloplasties like the De Vega or Kay repairs suffer high rates of late recurrence. Implanting a true prosthetic ring remodels the annulus and provides reliable long-term competence.
steps.tx: Implantation of a rigid or semi-rigid **prosthetic annuloplasty ring** demonstrates superior long-term durability and freedom from recurrent regurgitation compared to historical suture techniques. Suture methods such as the **De Vega annuloplasty** or **Kay repair** experience progressive suture pull-through, late annular redilatation, and recurrent regurgitation.

left.title: Prosthetic Ring Annuloplasty
points: Rigid or semi-rigid three-dimensional conformational design
High long-term freedom from recurrent severe regurgitation

right.title: Suture Annuloplasty Techniques
points: Employs purse-string or bicuspidizing suture plication
Sutures cheese-wire through fragile fatty annular tissue
High rate of recurrence within 3 to 5 years

steps.say: Place sutures with extreme caution near the triangle of Koch. The atrioventricular node and bundle of His lie just superior to the coronary sinus ostium along the septal annulus. Suture placement must avoid deep bites in this danger zone to prevent complete heart block.
steps.tx: Suture placement along the septal annulus within the **triangle of Koch** requires extreme surgical vigilance to protect the **atrioventricular node** and proximal **bundle of His**. Sutures must be kept superficial or transitioned onto the base of the anterior leaflet to eliminate postoperative complete heart block.

nodes.label: Identify coronary sinus ostium and tendon of Todaro
Delineate anatomical apex of triangle of Koch
Place superficial sutures away from AV node and His bundle
Secure prosthetic annuloplasty ring safely onto tricuspid annulus

steps.say: When valve replacement is unavoidable, implant a bioprosthetic valve. The low-pressure, low-velocity right heart circulation carries an exceptionally high risk of mechanical valve thrombosis. Bioprosthetic replacement avoids this catastrophe and provides excellent hemodynamics.
steps.tx: When severe structural destruction mandates **tricuspid replacement**, a **bioprosthetic valve** is strongly preferred over a mechanical prosthesis. The low-pressure, sluggish hemodynamic flow in the right-sided cardiac chambers predisposes mechanical valves to acute **mechanical valve thrombosis**, resulting in catastrophic valve stuckness and high mortality.

rows: Avoided; reserved only for rare re-replacement with warfarin compliance

steps.say: Carcinoid heart disease damages right-sided heart valves through circulating serotonin. Vasoactive peptides produce dense fibrous plaques on tricuspid leaflets and subvalvular cords. Leaflets become stiff, thickened, and retracted, requiring complete excision and bioprosthetic valve replacement.
steps.tx: **Carcinoid heart disease** produces dense **fibrous plaques** on the endocardial surfaces of tricuspid leaflets and chordae tendineae. Serotonin and vasoactive mediators cause rigid, **retracted leaflets** that fail to coapt, producing severe mixed stenosis and regurgitation requiring complete surgical excision and bioprosthetic replacement.

nodes.label: Hepatic metastases release massive systemic serotonin and kinins
Fibroblast proliferation forms dense plaque on right-sided endocardium
Fixed retracted tricuspid leaflets produce severe regurgitation
Perform surgical bioprosthetic tricuspid valve replacement

steps.say: In Ebstein anomaly, the modern cone repair reconstructs a functional tricuspid valve. The surgeon mobilizes and delaminates adhered leaflet tissue from the right ventricular wall, creating a 360-degree circumferential tissue cone. Anchoring this cone at the true anatomical annulus restores leaflet coaptation.
steps.tx: In adult patients with symptomatic **Ebstein anomaly**, the modern surgical standard is the **cone repair** described by da Silva. The procedure employs extensive surgical **delamination** of abnormally adherent leaflet tissue, constructing a 360-degree circumferential leaflet cone anchored to the true anatomical tricuspid annulus.
